name: Runtime_CopyAndCallRoutine
algorithm: Allocates a fixed-size executable buffer, DMA-copies a ROM routine into it, calls the copied routine through the r6 call veneer, then frees the buffer.

family.evidence: Each sibling has the same allocator, three-word DMA setup, r6 indirect-call veneer, and free sequence; only its arguments, copy extent, or source vary.

credible_shapes_tried: volatile compound DMA-register aggregate assignment: canonical score unchanged
word-typed DMA-register aggregate assignment: canonical score unchanged
local three-word descriptor followed by assignment: emits a related LDMIA/STMIA copy, but adds a 12-byte stack object (80 versus 72 bytes; 36 differing halfwords)
volatile and ordinary word-pointer post-increment stores: retain the 72-byte extent but emit separate one-register stores rather than the reference grouped store
static inline three-scalar DMA publisher: retains scalar stores, grows to 76 versus 72 bytes, and scores 30 differing halfwords

shared StartDmaTransfer() inline helper (video_dma_family.h, same one 08003a7c uses), called both with pre-loaded locals in source/destination/control order and with inline literal arguments: both lower to three separate one-register str instructions, 72 bytes, 16 differing halfwords (worse than the plain field-store baseline, and still no stmia)

compound-literal aggregate store `*dma = (struct DmaChannel){src, dst, ctl};` through the same non-volatile pointer: byte-identical candidate output to the plain per-field store baseline (72 bytes, 13 differing halfwords) -- confirms the aggregate-assignment shapes above reduce to the same field-by-field lowering

reordering the three dma-> field assignment statements (destination-first, and other orderings) and moving the dma-pointer computation earlier: no effect on emitted bytes for the reachable orderings (byte-identical to baseline), or strictly worse when the dma pointer is forced to survive the Func_08004938 call (80 bytes, needs an extra callee-saved register)
compiler_backend_evidence: Read alchemy-gcc/gs1cc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c and arm.md directly: the STM-combining logic that could explain the reference's single `stmia r3!, {r0,r1,r2}` from three independently sourced words (store_multiple_sequence/emit_stm_seq, patterns *stmsi and *stmsi_postinc) is gated `TARGET_ARM` only (arm.md ~4990-5083); Thumb has no analogous peephole. The only Thumb multi-register store insns are movmem8b/movmem12b (thumb_expand_movstrqi, arm.md ~5111-5155; output routine thumb_output_move_mem_multiple, arm.c ~9425), and their asm template unconditionally emits a paired `ldmia`+`stmia` (a genuine block copy between two memory regions) as a single indivisible multi-set insn -- it can never emit the stmia half alone. This is independent of volatility (the ARM-only peephole additionally excludes MEM_VOLATILE_P operands, but that exclusion never even applies to Thumb, which has no candidate peephole regardless). Given no Thumb-reachable machine pattern in this compiler route folds three independently computed register values into one STM without a paired load, the reference's standalone grouped store looks structurally unemittable from ordinary field-store or aggregate-store C on this compiler; this matches, and mechanically explains, the 'canonical score unchanged' results recorded above.
remaining: The reference groups the source, allocated destination, and control word in a writeback three-register store, then restores the DMA base. Canonical ordinary-C shapes instead keep those values in a nonconsecutive allocation or introduce a stack descriptor. GCC 2.96's Thumb block-copy path explains the local-descriptor LDMIA/STMIA result, but does not account for the reference's standalone grouped store. Compiler-source inspection (see compiler_backend_evidence) shows Thumb has no store-multiple peephole outside the always-paired LDMIA/STMIA block-copy pattern, so no ordinary field-store or aggregate-store C shape reaches the reference's lone STM. The shared original DMA-write source shape remains unknown; neither adoption nor a permanent compiler classification is justified from this evidence alone.
notes: Measured only in the complete canonical video-dma-queue translation unit; no per-owner flags were used.
No inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, forbidden ABI, copied instruction bytes, or compiler modification was used.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes.
